title: Best Black and Decker Dehumidifier (2026): 20, 30 & 50-Pint
dek: The power-tool brand sells four ENERGY STAR dehumidifiers, a clean recall record and some of the widest price swings we've seen on one model.
description: The best Black and Decker dehumidifier for each space, from the 20-pint BDT20WTB to the 50-pint pump model, plus button, manual and recall answers.
intro: A **Black and Decker dehumidifier** might not be the first thing you think of from a brand known for drills and leaf blowers, but Black+Decker's current U.S. lineup covers the essentials: four models in 20-, 30- and 50-pint sizes, all ENERGY STAR certified according to the brand's own product pages. For most basements, our pick is the **50-Pint with Pump (BDT50PWTB)**, which drains itself instead of filling a bucket.

Two things are worth knowing before you shop. First, Black+Decker doesn't appear on either of the two largest dehumidifier recalls in U.S. history, which together covered dozens of other brand names. Second, pricing on the same model can vary wildly between retailers — we've seen the 30-pint list for nearly twice as much at one store as at another — so comparison shopping pays off here more than usual.
topPicksLead: The **Black+Decker 50-Pint with Pump (BDT50PWTB)** is the best choice for most basements because its built-in pump lets it run for weeks without a bucket to empty.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (BDT50PWTB)
pros: Rated for up to 4,500 sq ft
cons: Costs noticeably more than the non-pump 50-pint
products.whyWeLoveIt: In a basement where the nearest drain sits higher than the unit, a pump is what turns a dehumidifier from a chore into an appliance you can forget about. This is the only Black+Decker model that has one.
products.performance: It's rated at 50 pints a day with coverage up to 4,500 square feet, Black+Decker's largest. The pump pushes water out through a hose rather than relying on the 14.3-pint internal bucket, and a top-mounted panel with an LED readout lets you set a target anywhere from 35% to 80%. For more pump-equipped choices across brands, see our [dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

The catch is price: we've seen this exact model listed at one big-box store for nearly half what another retailer charged. Check several sellers before you buy. Not sure whether 30 pints is enough? Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) walks through the math.

blocks.text: We don't run a lab. We compare each model's capacity, coverage, bucket size and humidistat range from Black+Decker's spec sheets, confirm ENERGY STAR status, search CPSC recall records, and read owner reviews for recurring issues like pump failures, noisy fans or inaccurate humidity readings.
We also track pricing patterns across retailers — not to quote prices, which change daily, but because a model that swings wildly in price changes which pick represents real value.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Black+Decker dehumidifier

items.label: Coverage, not just pints
items.text: Both 50-pint models top out at 4,500 square feet. Beyond that, you need a second unit or a [whole-house system](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/).

items.label: Pump or no pump
items.text: The pump model costs more but lets you skip emptying a 14.3-pint bucket. Worth it if the nearest drain is higher than the unit.

items.label: Price across retailers
items.text: Check at least three sellers. The same Black+Decker model can vary by close to double.

items.label: ENERGY STAR on the listing
items.text: All current models are certified per the brand; confirm the exact model number on the retailer's page.

items.label: Rival budget brands
items.text: Compare against Frigidaire, hOmeLabs and Midea in our [best budget dehumidifier](/best/best-budget-dehumidifier/) guide before you buy.

blocks.text: That's not a promise a Black+Decker unit will never be recalled — just the current public record. If you're buying secondhand, look up the exact model number on CPSC.gov regardless of brand.

sections.heading: Black and Decker dehumidifier manual and buttons

blocks.text: The model number (BDT20WTB, BDT30WTB, BDT50WTB or BDT50PWTB) is on the label on the back of the unit. Search that number on Black+Decker's appliance support pages or the retailer's listing to download the owner's manual.
Exact labels vary by model, so check your manual, but a typical Black+Decker panel includes:

items: **Power:** turns the unit on and off.
**Up/down arrows:** set your target humidity, usually in 5% steps; the display shows the room reading the rest of the time.
**Fan speed:** toggles between high and low.
**Timer:** sets an automatic on or off time.
**Mode or continuous:** on some models, runs the unit nonstop regardless of the humidistat — useful only for drying out a wet space.
**Filter light:** reminds you to rinse the washable filter; hold the indicated button to reset it afterward.

blocks.title: Good starting setting
blocks.text: Set the humidistat to 45–50% and the fan to auto or high. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has seasonal targets.

sections.heading: Are Black and Decker dehumidifiers good?

blocks.text: They're solid, conventional compressor units with ENERGY STAR certification and a clean recall record. What they don't offer is anything you can't get elsewhere: no Wi-Fi, no collapsible design, no extended warranty. That makes the buying decision mostly about price on the day you shop.

If you find a Black+Decker at a genuinely good price, it's a sensible buy. If it's priced at the top of its range, a better-equipped rival may cost the same. Our [energy-efficient dehumidifier](/best/best-energy-efficient-dehumidifier/) guide lists the Most Efficient options.

For most basements, the **Black+Decker 50-Pint with Pump (BDT50PWTB)** is the one to buy: full 4,500-square-foot coverage and a pump that drains it for you. The **20-Pint (BDT20WTB)** is the right size for a bedroom or apartment, the **30-Pint (BDT30WTB)** fits mid-size rooms if you find it at a fair price, and the **50-Pint (BDT50WTB)** saves money if a floor drain is nearby. Whichever you choose, shop several retailers — the price differences are real.

faqs.q: What is the best Black and Decker dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For basements, the 50-Pint with Pump (BDT50PWTB), which covers up to 4,500 square feet and drains itself. For a bedroom or small apartment, the 20-Pint (BDT20WTB).

faqs.q: Is the Black and Decker 4,500 sq ft dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: Both 50-pint models are rated for 4,500 square feet. The pump version (BDT50PWTB) is worth the extra cost if your drain is higher than the unit; otherwise the BDT50WTB with a gravity hose offers the same coverage for less.

faqs.q: Where can I find a Black and Decker dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Find the model number on the label on the back of the unit, then search it on Black+Decker's appliance support pages or the retailer's product listing to download the PDF manual.

faqs.q: What do the buttons on a Black and Decker dehumidifier do?
faqs.a: Typically: power, up/down arrows to set target humidity, fan speed, timer, and on some models a continuous mode. A filter light reminds you to rinse the filter. Check your model's manual for the exact labels.

faqs.q: Are Black and Decker dehumidifiers any good?
faqs.a: Yes, as straightforward ENERGY STAR compressor units with a clean recall history. They lack smart features and extended warranties, so they're best bought when the price is competitive with Midea, Frigidaire and hOmeLabs.

faqs.q: Has Black and Decker had a dehumidifier recall?
faqs.a: Black+Decker doesn't appear on the large Gree (2013) or New Widetech (2021) recalls, which covered dozens of other brand names. Still, check any secondhand unit's model number on CPSC.gov.

faqs.q: Who makes Black and Decker dehumidifiers?
faqs.a: Black+Decker licenses its name for home appliances, so the dehumidifiers are made by a licensed partner rather than the tool division. Check the manual or ENERGY STAR listing for your model's manufacturer details.
